capture_source: live capture 2026-09-01; SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP (A4H) kernel 793. Reply to RFC_READ_TABLE with QUERY_TABLE=DD03L, DELIMITER='|', ROWCOUNT=2000. Sanitised: the 8-byte GW conversation handle at offset 40 is zeroed in both frames, same byte length, so every offset and length field stays valid. The bodies are SAPCOMPRESS-compressed table rows and contain no hostname, SID, user name or address - the only ASCII runs in 53673 bytes were the handle and the string 'ET_DATA'. NI length prefixes stripped.
evidence: the two frames were read consecutively from one socket; joining their bodies gives 53513 bytes that walk cleanly to the 0xFFFF terminator with 2 bytes trailing, which neither frame does alone

files.multiframe_read_table_part1.bin: 28080 bytes, GW type 0x06cb. Body 28000 B. The TLV walk consumes 27799 B and stops needing 250 bytes of a 0x0305 record with 197 left - in sync, simply out of data.
files.multiframe_read_table_part2.bin: 25593 bytes, GW type 0x0609. Body 25513 B. NOT a TLV stream: it begins mid-record, with the remaining bytes of the 0x0305 record part1 was cut inside. Walking it standalone fails immediately on a bogus tag 0x1d5e.

notes: This is the capture that established multi-frame responses. Before it, Connection.call issued exactly one recv_message() per invoke, so any reply larger than one gateway frame failed with 'malformed TLV: tag 0x0305 length 250 exceeds remaining payload (197 bytes)' - and, worse, left the remainder queued on the socket for the next call to misread.
The bodies concatenate directly. There is no per-frame trailer, no length preamble on the continuation, and no re-framing: part2 is the literal continuation of part1's byte stream.

Bytes 56-59 are a BE uint32 giving THIS frame's payload length: 28000 and 25513, matching exactly. Verified against 9 other golden fixtures where it also equals the body length on every server response, and reads 0 on client requests. The doc previously mapped 52-63 as an RFC library name string, which these frames disprove - the region is three BE uint32.

[ASSUMED] no header field is confirmed to mean 'more follows'. Two looked like it and both are wrong. Bytes 17-20 (BE int32) read -1 on part1 and 500 on part2; bytes 60-63 read 0 and 1. They are the same signal - identical across all 13 frames compared - and both ALSO fire on signon_incomplete_752_response.bin and cpic_logon_error_response.bin, which are complete terminal replies with nothing following. A reassembly loop driven by either would hang on a failed logon waiting for a frame that never comes. Reassembly is therefore driven by the stream's own 0xFFFF terminator. A three-frame capture would settle what those fields actually mean: the middle frame's values would show whether they track continuation or something that merely coincides with it here.

The capture continued past part2 with 40 identical 80-byte frames of GW type 0x06ce - a bare GW header plus RFC marker, zero TLV payload. What produces them is not established. They contribute nothing to reassembly and the loop stops before reaching them, but a reader that kept going on an empty frame would spin rather than progress, which is why one is refused explicitly.
